$schemaNote: Oracle-triangulation record: OLV point-cloud registration vs ANALYTIC TRUTH — a KNOWN rigid transform. Cloud Q is built from an asymmetric source cloud P by a known rotation+translation; OLV's registration must recover that same transform. No third-party registration tool (Open3D/CloudCompare) is available, so the truth anchor is the closed-form known transform itself, not a matched implementation. OLV's leg is recomputed LIVE by tests/oracleConsensusRegistration.test.ts from the same fixtures (the JSON only records the known transform the test must recover). Convention: source->target — the recovered (R,t) satisfy q ~= R*p + t, exactly the transform that generated Q. Two cases use different small rotations, axes and translations so a single systematic error could not pass both.

contract.algorithm: trimmed ICP with closed-form Kabsch/Horn rigid solve (src/registration/generalIcp -> rigidSolve), identity initialisation, full correspondence (Q is P transformed, so every point has an exact partner)
contract.convention: source->target: recovered R,t satisfy q ~= R*p + t (the same transform that built Q from P)
contract.fixture: asymmetric synthetic cloud (200 points, deterministic LCG, extents 10x6x3 m; NOT symmetric/degenerate so R is uniquely determined)
contract.convergenceAssumption: small transform (rotation <=5 deg) so ICP converges from an identity initial pose to the global optimum

fixture.model: P = deterministic asymmetric cloud; Q = R(rz=4,ry=3,rx=2 deg)*P + [0.5,-0.3,0.2]

oracles.tool: closed-form: Q constructed from P by a known rigid transform

fixture.model: P = deterministic asymmetric cloud; Q = R(rz=1,ry=-2,rx=3 deg)*P + [-1.2,0.8,-0.5]

oracles.tool: closed-form: Q constructed from P by a known rigid transform
